newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: China says hurdle still too high on WTO membership.
newsitem.headline: China says hurdle still too high on WTO membership.

text.p: Chinese Trade Minister Wu Yi said on Sunday the hurdle for China to enter the World Trade Organisation (WTO) was still too high, Japanese trade ministry officials said.

In talks in Manila with Japanese Trade Minister Shinji Sato, Wu urged WTO members to ease their conditions for China's membership -- one of the key issues at the WTO conference in Singapore next month.
Wu and Sato took part in the ministerial conference of the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in Manila.
"The signatories to the WTO should lower their requests to China," a senior Japanese trade minstry official quoted Wu as telling Sato. "We in turn will make our best efforts."

Wu was referring to demands by many WTO members such as Japan and the United States for China to ease tariffs and other restrictions on imports, especially on cars, electronic goods and other industrial products, and on services, such as financial business and distribution, said the Japanese official, who took part in Sunday's talks.
Wu said the atmosphere within the WTO changed significantly last month in a formal meeting on China held in Geneva from October 30 to November 1.
China told the Geneva meeting it would not add further trade restrictions while the WTO considered its membership.
